Done. All three deliverables are in place under `out/`, plus the input file at the working-directory root.

**What was produced**

- `shibei_week42.json` — the brief's JSON block saved verbatim; verified to parse and match the brief byte-for-byte in content.
- `out/文书.docx` — a one-page Chinese weekly report (拾贝书店周报): centered title, period subtitle, a 3-row label/value table (部门 / 填报人 / 报送日期), then four numbered sections. Body is 12pt SimSun black at 1.3× line spacing, section headings are bold SimHei via real heading styles, and a centered page-number footer runs in the bottom margin.
- `out/fields.json` — the field ledger: required/optional field lists, per-field status and normalized value, plus an explicit record of every normalization applied.
- `out/delivery-report.json` — exactly four keys, nothing more or less.

**Data handling.** The input had three deliberate defects, all normalized and logged rather than silently passed through: `部门` carried leading/trailing spaces (trimmed to 拾贝书店), `本周工作内容[1]` was whitespace-only, and `问题与需协调事项[1]` was an empty string. Both empty list items were dropped — the rendered report shows 2 work items and 1 coordination item, with numbering running 1/2 and 1/1 rather than leaving gaps.

**Report contents.** Since every required and optional field resolved to a real value and no input key fell outside the weekly-report field set, the three list keys are all empty and `title` is `拾贝书店周报`. That is what the ledger says, so that is what was written.

**One judgment call worth flagging:** the brief did not specify which fields the weekly-report template treats as required vs. optional, and this baseline arm has no template asset mounted. I used a standard split — 部门 / 填报人 / 周期 / 本周工作内容 / 下周工作计划 / 报送日期 as required, and 问题与需协调事项 / 温馨提示 as optional (the note slot). `温馨提示` was the most debatable: I recognized it as the report's note field rather than an unrecognized key. If your house template says otherwise, `unknown_keys` is where it would surface. The split is declared in one place in `gen_reports.py` (`REQUIRED` / `OPTIONAL`) if you want to change it.

**Verification.** `postcheck.py` passed 9/9 with zero errors or warnings. LibreOffice rendered the file to a single page with all text intact and no blank pages. 20 assertions on the JSON key shape, cross-file title consistency, trimming, and docx text content all passed. Note that the `documents:visual-judge` subagent could not launch — the provider registry rejected it — so I inspected the rendered page image myself as the documented fallback; it is clean.

Working files `gen_doc.js` and `gen_reports.py` are left alongside the deliverables so the run is reproducible; the scratch render directory was cleaned up.
